jHub.title: Let AI do tasks (overview)
jHub.body:
Say what the job is, pick a fitting agent, then check what it hands back.

📍 Location: App overview › Let AI do tasks › Let AI do tasks (overview)
⚙️ Usage layer: no model parameters change, only how you use it
🧪 Try it:

🎯 Role

  • Matches seven common jobs (code, writing, research, spreadsheets, images and video, repeating chores, study) with fitting products.

▶ How to use it

  • Name the job → choose “with you” or “on its own” → pick a product → give material and rules → check the result.

🧠 Why it’s designed this way (the logic underneath)

Things called “AI” differ a lot; the right pick saves half the effort.

✅ Why this works

Pays off most on repetitive, fiddly or research-heavy jobs.

⚠️ Limits / notes: It makes mistakes and can make things up; check anything that matters yourself.

jPick.title: Pick an agent by task
jPick.body:
For one job, first decide: should the AI work step by step with you, or take the task and finish it alone?

📍 Location: App overview › Let AI do tasks › Pick an agent by task
⚙️ Usage layer: no model parameters change, only how you use it
🧪 Try it:

🎯 Role

  • With you: you watch every step and steer (editor, chat). On its own: once briefed it runs and hands back a result (background, scheduled).

▶ How to use it

  • New to it or it matters: start with “with you”; for repeat jobs you can check, let go.

🧠 Why it’s designed this way (the logic underneath)

The more you let go, the more you must brief first and check after.

✅ Why this works

The right mode means less rework.

⚠️ Limits / notes: Products change fast; one product may offer both.

jCheck.title: Check its output
jCheck.body:
What the AI hands back is like a classmate’s homework: it counts only after you mark it.

📍 Location: App overview › Let AI do tasks › Check its output
⚙️ Usage layer: no model parameters change, only how you use it
🧪 Try it:

🎯 Role

  • Run tests on code; compare numbers with the source table; open cited sources; check images and video for errors and rights.

▶ How to use it

  • Let it work on a copy or a new branch; never send it passwords, ID numbers or company secrets.

🧠 Why it’s designed this way (the logic underneath)

A model can be confidently wrong, and it looks right.

✅ Why this works

A few minutes of checking stops most errors.

⚠️ Limits / notes: In a field you do not know, errors are hard to spot; ask someone who does.
